Unpacking Suboxone Lawsuits and the Legal Battle in 2024 

The Suboxone lawsuit revolves around the allegation that the defendants, including Indivior Inc. and Aquestive Therapeutics, Inc., were aware of the risk of severe tooth decay and other dental injuries associated with Suboxone use. Plaintiffs argue that these risks were not effectively communicated to prescribing doctors or patients, leading to a lack of informed consent. This failure to provide adequate warnings, they claim, was driven by profit motives. [1]  

The core legal issue here is whether the defendants fulfilled their responsibility to warn patients and healthcare providers about the potential dental risks associated with Suboxone. The plaintiffs argue that despite being aware of these risks, the defendants did not take adequate action to prevent dental injuries. The recent addition of a warning about tooth decay associated with Suboxone by the FDA in January 2022 lends credibility to the plaintiffs’ claims. 

A Turning Point in Suboxone Tooth Decay Lawsuits 

As of January 26, 2024, the Suboxone lawsuit is at a crucial juncture. A hearing was held recently to determine whether the litigation should become an MDL (Multi-District Litigation) class action lawsuit. The expectation is that the MDL Panel will consolidate all Suboxone lawsuits in federal court in Ohio, which could significantly streamline the legal process. [2] 

The defendants in the Suboxone lawsuits include Indivior Inc., Indivior Solutions Inc. and Aquestive Therapeutics, Inc. These companies are accused of various forms of wrongful and negligent conduct related to the development, design, testing, labeling, packaging, promoting and selling of Suboxone. 

Administrative Challenges in Handling Mass Tort Cases 

Managing mass tort cases in a law firm can be daunting due to their sheer volume and complexity.  

First, there’s the issue of information overload, as firms must collect, organize and manage extensive documentation and data related to numerous plaintiffs. Coordinating communication and updates with many clients can be challenging, potentially leading to delays and misunderstandings. 

Additionally, litigation logistics, such as filing numerous lawsuits, managing court appearances and coordinating settlements, require a high level of organization and resources. Law firms handling mass tort cases must also be prepared for the potential influx of inquiries, which can strain existing administrative processes.
